case_name: Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited, Jammu v Teja Singh
respondent:
Teja Singh
Supreme Court of India

16 January 2009
Civil Appeal No. 292 of 2009 [Arising out of SLP(C) No. 7803/2006]
The Order of the Court was as follows :
Leave granted.
1.  The respondent was employed with the appellant company as a daily-rated Mazdoor. He was recruited in the year 1973. He was appointed on regular basis with effect from 11.8.1986. He attained the age of superannuation on 30th August, 1989. Thereafter, again while working on daily-wages, his services were terminated in 1993. He filed a representation for payment of gratuity as also other retiral benefits. He having been denied the retiral benefits on the premise that he had not completed 10 years' qualifying service as required in terms of the Service Rules, he filed an original application before the Central Administrative Tribunal.

facts: The respondent was employed with the appellant company as a daily-rated Mazdoor.
He was recruited in the year 1973.
He was appointed on regular basis with effect from 11.8.1986.
He attained the age of superannuation on 30th August, 1989.
Thereafter, again while working on daily-wages, his services were terminated in 1993.
issues: Whether the regularisation scheme formulated by the appellant company in 1989 was enforceable
Whether the respondent's services could be regularised despite not completing 10 years' qualifying service
petitioner_arguments: The regularisation scheme formulated by the appellant company in 1989 was enforceable and the respondent's services should be regularised
The Constitution Bench decision in Umadevi (3) and Ors. vs. Umadevi (2006) did not apply to this case
respondent_arguments: The regularisation scheme formulated by the appellant company in 1989 was not enforceable and the respondent's services should not be regularised
The Constitution Bench decision in Umadevi (3) and Ors. vs. Umadevi (2006) applied to this case
court_reasoning: The Constitution Bench decision in Umadevi (3) and Ors. vs. Umadevi (2006) held that regularisation or permanent continuance of temporary, contractual, casual, daily-wage or ad hoc employees dehors the Constitutional scheme is impermissible in law
The High Courts should not issue directions for absorption, regularisation, or permanent continuance unless the recruitment itself was made regularly and in terms of the Constitutional scheme
holding: The impugned judgment is set aside and the appeal is allowed accordingly
cases_cited: by a three-Judge Bench of this Court in Official Liquidator vs. Dayanand
